=== Useful links ===
* [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imbolc Wikipedia] mainly discusses the traditional Gaelic festival, with a bit on neopaganism at the bottom
** "Celebrations often involved hearthfires, special foods, divination or watching for omens, candles or a bonfire if the weather permitted."
** The festival focused on the goddess Brigid (Christianized as St. Brigid), who "represented the light half of the year, and the power that will bring people from the dark season of winter into spring..."
* [http://www.crizmac.com/artandsoul/index.php/2011/02/02/make-st-brigids-cross/ How to make a St. Brigid's cross], preferably out of reeds or rushes
* [https://atheopaganism.wordpress.com/2015/01/29/an-atheopagan-life-celebrating-riverain-and-adapting-the-wheel-of-the-year/ Riverain: an Atheopagan alternative], includes hiking in the rain (could be appropriate for the Pacific Northwest's rainy winters, less so for snowy Ottawa)

== Strategic planning ==
=== One page plan? ===
Brandon wants to see if what we wrote for the core values, beliefs, purpose, etc still works

====Core Values/Beliefs====
* '''All [[life]] is precious.'''  This is the root of our value system.  Respecting and cherishing life is the reason for everything we do.
* '''[[The Destiny]] of SolSeed is to take root amongst the stars.'''  To protect the future of life, we must help it grow beyond [[Earth]] and even beyond the [[Sol]]ar system, so it can never be wiped out.  More importantly, our belief in this audaciously optimistic goal, and in the epic story of a future with life thriving on many worlds, is central to defining the [[SolSeed Movement]].
* '''We ALL are precious [[SolSeed]].'''  SolSeed is defined as "the body of all life on Earth," encompassing every human culture and belief system as well as all other species.  This connects particularly to the "Openness/welcoming differences" practice below.
* '''Science as the way to know truth.'''  We believe in the scientific worldview, the principle that observing the world is a far better route to knowledge than religious texts and magical thinking.  We talk about [[Gaia]], a controversial scientific concept, and about a Destiny that sounds like a prophecy, but we admit that these are stories, not knowledge.  We believe in the Destiny as a worthy and inspiring goal and Gaia as a useful and inspiring metaphor, but what we believe to be ''true'' (or rather, as close to the truth as we can presently get) is based around mainstream science.

Life is Precious
* Cherish the Earth
* Embrace Science
* Live in Community
* Bring Life to the Galaxy

==== Actions ====
* Build a SolSeed village/society: on hold … could work toward it through small steps like hikes and game nights with interested Portlanders
* Become a player in the <s>space industry</s> Pagan community: Gaia statue kickstarter, etc
* Incorporate the SolSeed Society nonprofit to do or contribute to charitable work: dormant
* Promulgate our ideas through various media: Kickstarters can help with this
* Do something that makes people take us seriously: tree-climbing robot, Gaia statue shrines, maybe a book or making Gaia.Wiki more exciting with a community of contributors

=== Social Media and other Connectors ===
* We currently update Facebook irregularly, maybe an average of once every 10 days or so
** We've had a few comment-thread conversations but not much else to show for it
* We have zero Twitter presence
* Our Meetups each have ~30-40 members (except Gaia's People Ottawa has 72) but only rarely attract new people to events … Brandon thinks they have a lot of potential
** The Portland SolSeed ''Seeing Nature'' reading group got some people
** Gaia's People Ottawa doesn't ask new members to answer questions, and may not require Eric's approval for people to join (but we probably haven't rejected any requests to join the other groups)
** Interesting strategy: join other Meetup groups and create events on their pages for our events
* Ben has identified several people he should contact and then not done anything about it
* Drip emails
* Videos, esp. [[Gaia's Heartbeat]]
